title: As Wardogs blows past 200k Steam concurrents, its developers are prepared for the day 'hype dies down'
summary: "Doesn't make it a bad game, or even a problem."
body: The way our hobby talks about player counts is all sorts of messed up. Steam concurrents are a useful metric for gauging a game's general popularity, but they paint an incomplete picture. They're a single data point, yet have become the flimsy scaffolding on which the internet builds elaborate headcanon about a game's quality, viability, or deadness. Sometimes dogpiling is so successful, and the resulting perception so difficult to fight, that simply saying a game is dead is enough to help kill it. It's a trend that annoys me to no end, so it's refreshing to see a developer speaking openly about concurrents—both about how many it considers "healthy," and why it's normal for the number to rise and fall. It's been a recurring topic for Wardogs developer Bulkhead, whose closed beta surpassed 200,000 concurrents today on Steam. Responding to a TimTheTatman clip on X, CEO Joe Brammer spoke on the milsim's unexpected popularity, and its inevitable (but healthy) decline. Civ 7's had kind of a rough go of things since it launched in early 2025. It made some big changes to the formula that didn't go over well with a significant portion of the fan base, the UI was almost universally unpopular, and performance was dodgy. Firaxis has been banging away on it ever since, to mixed results: A major update released in May brought a big bump in player numbers on Steam, but the reactions expressed via Steam reviews were almost literally split down the middle. title: Me: You can now run DLSS 5 on AMD GPUs. My RX 9070 XT: Please stop, it hurts us
summary: A new app allows you to inject DLSS Neural Rendering deep into games even if you're running an AMD card. You probably won't want to, though.
body: Another day, another DLSS 5 story that actually kinda doesn't involve Nvidia itself doing anything, because it seems now AMD GPU owners can get in on the act. A new homebrew app has been released on Github that will allow you to run the DLSS Neural Rendering feature on a Radeon GPU. I've tried it and it works, but damn does it hurt the poor Radeon silicon. From having DLSS 5 .dll files plucked from an early access version of NBA 2K27, we've had modders working hard to create surprisingly polished ways to essentially get the tech working in practically any game , even if it doesn't natively support traditional DLSS itself. I've been playing around with it a lot this past week, even to the point of jamming it into Football Manager 26 just to see what would happen. And, y'know what, I kinda like the result so I'm keeping it. I wasn't expecting that, and I also wasn't expecting this technology, created by Nvidia, to appear so quickly on AMD GPUs. Historically we've found that where Nvidia goes, so AMD follows, at least in the GPU feature space, but it seems like AMD might not actually have to do much this time. summary: ماذا يحدث لفريق العاصمة؟
body: ماذا يحدث لفريق العاصمة؟ بعدما أفلت باريس سان جيرمان من الخسارة في أول جولتين، واقتنص تعادلًا2-2  أمام رين، ثم كرر السيناريو أمام ليل بالنتيجة نفسها، لم يتمكن حامل لقب الدوري الفرنسي من إنقاذ نفسه هذه المرة، وسقط في فخ الخسارة أمام موناكو بنتيجة (1-2) على ملعب "حديقة الأمراء" بالجولة الثالثة من الليجا كان باريس قد احتاج إلى عودة متأخرة أمام ليل، بعدما سجل فيتينيا وماركينيوس هدفين خلال الوقت بدل الضائع لانتزاع التعادل، بعدما كان متأخرًا بهدفين، لكن موناكو حرم الفريق الباريسي من تكرار سيناريو النجاة، وحافظ على تقدمه حتى صافرة النهاية. تقدم باريس سان جيرمان أولًا عن طريق قائده ماركينيوس، قبل أن يقلب موناكو المواجهة في الشوط الثاني بتسجيل هدفين، ليخرج بانتصار ثمين من ملعب حامل اللقب، ويعمق أزمة الفريق الباريسي الذي لا يزال يبحث عن انتصاره الأول في الدوري هذا الموسم. وهكذا، تحولت البداية المتعثرة لباريس من تعادلين بطعم النجاة إلى خسارة كاملة، بعدما لم تسعفه العودة المتأخرة هذه المرة، ليتلقى لويس إنريكي ضربة مبكرة في حملة الدفاع عن لقب الدوري الفرنسي.

body: Ever since the Control mod appeared I've been enjoying jamming the released DLSS 5 .dll files into a bunch of different games, to greater or lesser effect. Some games it works well in, some it doesn't quite take and you end up with visuals that look a lot like the characters have worms writhing around under their skin. Though, I have to say when I stuck it into the review version of The Blood of Dawnwalker and it failed to hook the DLSS pipeline that look kinda worked for my semi-Vrakhiri. Bit of extra undead chic with the game failing to run the DLSS neural rendering feature with actual motion vectors or scene depth. Most things are getting more and more expensive, but crucially, not all things. Components like headsets and gamepads conform to the fast antiquating dictum that, with time, value will rise while costs decrease. That's pretty much the case with the Corsair HS35 v3. At the level of raw specs at least, Corsair's new mid-range headset has a touch more to offer than the SteelSeries Arctic Nova 3X, which is our favourite mid-range gaming headset. It came bearing a $90 price tag at launch (though you wouldn't pay full price for it in 2026). Like the Arctis Nova 3X, the HS35 v3 has 2.4 GHz wireless connectivity, Bluetooth, and a wired option. It has a detachable mic, and reasonably comfortable memory foam ear cups. Both models have 50mm drivers and a 20Hz - 20kHz frequency response. But the HS35 v3 is 10 grams lighter and $10 cheaper. Shots fired!
